title: This was seriously was of weirdest and coolest musicals I’ve seen in ...
transcript: We have to talk about the queer Socrates musical because they're about to release a cast album almost four years after it premiered. The Hang is kind of a jazz opera with a maximalist drag sensibility, and it's by Matt Ray and the iconic visionary queer artist Taylor Mac. The premise is that Socrates is in the final hours of his life, and he requests to spend them with his friends discussing philosophy, hence “the hang.” Seeing the show live in early 2022 was a pretty captivating, albeit bizarre, fever dreamlike experience. It sort of existed outside any firm dramatic structure, where even though there was technically a premise and characters, it almost felt like a revue or a song cycle at times. It was deliberately anachronistic Where even though it like “takes place in Ancient Greece” a lot of the philosophy they were discussing was contemporary, including a lot of queer theory. And I found the jazz score really infectious and well-crafted, and it beautifully showcased this large ensemble, including the musicians, who often got to move around the space and get moments in the spotlight. The one thing that wasn't really a criticism, as much as a barrier for me is that I sometimes found it hard to follow the philosophical discussions themselves. I found them a bit dense, especially with the sensory overload of the music and production. But for that reason, I'm all the more excited to give it another listen now that we’re getting a cast album. It's set to release on November 3rd Tomorrow, as I'm posting this, but if you're watching this later, it's already out right now. It's set to release on Bandcamp I'm not sure if it's gonna be streaming elsewhere, but it's gonna be pretty epic with 28 tracks And they're releasing a vinyl double album. To celebrate the release, they’re also doing a one night only concert staging at Joe's Pub on November 3rd. But hey, if the album gets some attention, maybe the full production could come back? I don't know, I'm just putting it out there!
